name: Fluoxetine
summary: A long-acting, activating SSRI widely used for depression, OCD, and bulimia nervosa; the long half-life forgives missed doses but slows washout.
mechanism: Selectively inhibits serotonin reuptake via SERT, increasing serotonergic transmission.

dosing.adult: 20 mg once daily (morning); may increase after several weeks

safety.pregnancy: Generally considered relatively low risk, but data are limited — weigh against untreated depression.
safety.lactation: Enters breast milk; generally considered compatible with monitoring.
contraindications: Concurrent MAOI use (or within 5 weeks of stopping fluoxetine)
warnings: Black-box warning: increased suicidality in children, adolescents, and young adults (≤24 y) early in treatment
Serotonin syndrome with other serotonergic drugs
monitoring: Mood and suicidality, especially in young patients early in treatment
safety.overdose: Generally well tolerated; serotonin syndrome, vomiting, and tachycardia possible; seizures are rare.

clinicalPearls: Long half-life means ~5 weeks washout before starting an MAOI — plan switches carefully.
Potent CYP2D6 inhibitor — raises levels of TCAs, many antipsychotics, and other CYP2D6 substrates.
good: Depression, OCD, or bulimia where an activating SSRI with a forgiving long half-life is desired.
bad: Patients who need a quick washout for an MAOI switch, or who take several CYP2D6-metabolized drugs.
